title: Fire Emblem Had an American Anime Before It Had an American Game
hook:
In 1998 you could rent a dubbed Fire Emblem anime in the United States, five years before the first Fire Emblem game left Japan. The dub called Marth Prince Mars. Did you ever see the Fire Emblem anime?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Americans could watch a Fire Emblem anime in English five years before they could play a Fire Emblem game? In nineteen ninety six, Japan got a two episode Fire Emblem anime, with Nintendo credited for its cooperation. It adapted the opening chapters of Mystery of the Emblem, the Super Famicom game starring Marth. Only two episodes were ever made, and the story was never continued. Then in nineteen ninety eight, ADV Films released it on VHS in North America, both subtitled and dubbed. That tape was the first thing with the Fire Emblem name sold officially in the United States. The dub did not even call the hero Marth. He was Prince Mars, and the princess Caeda became Sheeda. American viewers had no game to compare it to, because no Fire Emblem game had ever left Japan. The first one to do so was the Game Boy Advance Fire Emblem in November of two thousand three. One thing from that anime did last. Marth's Japanese voice actor, Hikaru Midorikawa, has voiced him ever since, including in Super Smash Brothers. So if you rented a strange fantasy tape in the late nineties, you may have met Marth before almost anyone else in America. Did you ever see the Fire Emblem anime? Follow for more gaming history.
